Question: The real factors of \(x^2+4\) are:
Solution:
Here, “real factors” means a factorization into polynomials of positive degree with real coefficients; constant factors are excluded.

Because \(x^2+4\) has degree \(2\), a nontrivial factorization would have two linear factors: their degrees must add to \(2\). A real linear factor \(ax+b\), with \(a\ne0\), is zero at the real number \(x=-b/a\). Its product with any other polynomial would therefore be zero there.

But every real square is nonnegative, so for every real \(x\),
\[
x^2+4\ge4>0.
\]
Thus \(x^2+4\) has no real zero and hence no real linear factor. There is no nontrivial real factorization, choice E.
